title: Kelly Martin's 12-piece band, Detroit tenors and Baby Lawrence dancing
summary: In Kelly Martin's show band with Al McKibbon he heard Detroit tenors and Don Byas, and one night watched Baby Lawrence tap on the sidewalk.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So Kelly Martin, it was a 12-piece band, and Al McKibbon was in the band and Kelly was the leader and we had chorus girls and they'd bring that new act in every week, you know, and it was quite an experience for me. Course I could read, but it was a big town and then I began to hear guys. There was a guy like Lorenzo Lawson, he was a top tenor player in Detroit, and Moon Mullins and Lamont...and so I was gettin' around a little bit then and there was a joint where we could go and jam and then when the guys would come in like Basie, I think I was in Kelly Martin's Band...I think we worked there six or seven months. But, anyway, the guys would come in town and I got a chance to hear Don Byas in Basie's band and different ones would come in and I was, you know, gettin' to hear people, you know what I mean. It was a tremendous experience, but one of the biggest experiences was one night we was all in "Paradise Valley". We'd all got off from work and it was silence, I didn't hear a pin drop, but i heard these taps...he didn't even have on

taps, he had on his shoes. And it...ohhh...I'd never heard anything like that before in my life, getting into sound. Everybody had their head down and this man was tap dancin' on the sidewalk, up side the walls, over the fire hydrants and whatnot. I say, "Who in the world is this?" They said, "This is Baby Lawrence." I says, "My God!" Can you imagine a couple hundred people congregated in a corner and they ain't nobody sayin' nuthin' and listenin' to Baby Lawrence dance. Ohhhh!
